page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 31.0 GB of system memory. The instance includes a single NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture, providing 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. It does not include local storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear division between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The host CPU exhibits weak performance in general-purpose computing, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression benchmarks are weak to poor. However, the integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers strong performance for specialized workloads. Large-model LLM inference benchmarks show top-tier prompt processing speeds, reaching 1134.43 tokens per second on a 7B model, and strong text generation speeds at 33.96 tokens per second.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is the contrast between its modest CPU capabilities and its accelerated graphics hardware. While memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is average, database operations and general CPU physics tests score in the lower percentiles. Consequently, this instance is not cost-efficient for general-purpose CPU computing or high-throughput web serving. Instead, its value lies in providing access to a dedicated 16 GB GPU at a lower hardware tier, making it a cost-effective choice for workloads that offload processing to the GPU.

This instance is suited for small to medium machine learning inference tasks, such as running 7B parameter language models, where the GPU can be fully utilized. It is also appropriate for entry-level CUDA development, video transcoding, and lightweight graphics rendering. It is not recommended for CPU-heavy compilation, high-performance databases, or applications requiring fast local storage.
